players.product: data-center air-cooled & water-cooled chillers, CDUs (1.3 MW / 2.5 MW / 5 MW) and Nlyte DCIM

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results (CFO): reported sales were $4.8 billion, adjusted operating profit was $455 million (down 33%) and adjusted EPS was $0.34, with an overall 9% decline in organic growth driven by much lower volumes in higher-margin CSA residential and light commercial; Q4 free cash flow was about $900 million and full-year free cash flow about $2.1 billion. Commercial HVAC offset part of the decline: CSA Commercial sales were up 12% in Q4 and up over 25% for the year, and global commercial HVAC grew 14% in 2025 (the fifth consecutive year of double-digit commercial HVAC growth).
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 sales $4.8 billion; adjusted operating profit $455 million (down 33%); adjusted EPS $0.34; overall 9% decline in organic growth; Q4 free cash flow about $900 million; full-year free cash flow about $2.1 billion; global commercial HVAC up 14%; CSA Commercial up 12% in Q4, up over 25% for the year

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 orders (CEO/CFO): fourth quarter CSA data center orders were up more than five times; total company orders were up 16%, with global commercial HVAC orders up over 45% and CSA commercial orders up 80% "reflecting some large data center wins"; applied orders within CSA commercial more than tripled year over year. Management said it is "still in the early innings" of data center demand.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 CSA data center orders up more than five times; total company orders up 16%; global commercial HVAC orders up over 45%; CSA commercial orders increased 80%; CSA applied orders more than tripled

quarterly_data.signal: Data center sales: Carrier grew its data center business to around $1 billion in 2025, and the 2026 outlook has data centers up about 50%; asked about orders converting to 2026 revenue, the CEO said Carrier is guiding to 1 and a half billion for data centers this year, with delivery timing set by the customers it won (he would like more pulled in). The CFO guided global commercial HVAC to be up low to mid-single digits in the first half and up mid-teens in the second half; the back-half acceleration reflects conversion of data center wins and delivery of the broader commercial backlog.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 data center business around $1 billion; 2026 data centers up about 50% (guiding to 1 and a half billion); commercial HVAC first half up low to mid-single digits, second half up mid-teens

quarterly_data.signal: Initial 2026 outlook (CFO; the cost-savings figure is from the CEO): flat to low mid-single-digit organic growth with reported sales of approximately $22 billion (including a roughly $350 million headwind from the Riello exit) and adjusted EPS of approximately $2.8; total company adjusted operating profit about $3.4 billion, free cash flow approximately $2 billion (second-half weighted) and about $1.5 billion of share repurchases; the 2025 cost actions deliver over $100 million of savings in 2026. Q1 2026 guide: revenue about $5 billion with organic revenue down high single digits (CSA resi down over 20%), company operating margin about 10% and adjusted EPS about $0.50.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 adjusted operating profit about $3.4 billion; free cash flow approximately $2 billion; share repurchases about $1.5 billion; Q1 revenue about $5 billion, operating margin about 10%, adjusted EPS about $0.50

quarterly_data.signal: Chiller portfolio and share (CEO): "our expanded portfolio now addresses essentially all major data center chiller applications"; Carrier's share of water-cooled chillers has increased four times since spin, and its recently introduced Maglev bearing air-cooled chillers give a meaningful share opportunity there too ("Key differentiators include quick restart, free cooling, and leading at elevated ambient temperatures"); "a lot of our recent wins have been on the air-cooled side." Over the past couple of years Carrier expanded its commercial HVAC lab and chiller manufacturing capacity globally and added hundreds of technicians.
quarterly_data.figure: water-cooled chiller share increased four times since spin

quarterly_data.signal: CDUs for liquid cooling (CEO): Carrier introduced its first CDU in 2025 and plans higher-capacity CDUs up to five megawatts in 2026. It chose to produce its own CDU ("It's essentially a mini chiller") after looking at organic and inorganic options, while keeping VC stakes (including a percentage of a two-phase solution company printed as "Zutor Corp"). The one megawatt / 1.3 megawatt unit introduced last year has already won in the southern United States, and "We just got a handshake on a new one earlier this week" in South America; three and five megawatt units come out later this year. "No margin, drag at all from CDUs." On liquid cooling and Quantum Leap: "We're in the first inning."
quarterly_data.figure: 1.3 megawatt CDU introduced last year; three and a five megawatt coming out later this year; CDUs up to five megawatts in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: NVIDIA / Vera Rubin cooling (CEO, answering on NVIDIA's chiller comments): Carrier works very closely with NVIDIA (the teams met in Vegas that week) on a number of climate-optimized reference designs and on the chilling requirements for the future Vera Rubin chip. He said data centers will require a combination of liquid and traditional cooling and that Carrier is "confident that NVIDIA agrees with that." Comparing Blackwell and Vera Rubin, he said Vera Rubin chips will be more efficient and deliver a lot more output, but the inlet temperature will be about the same, so "both designs require the same amount of heat dissipation." Working closely with NVIDIA and with Carrier's own hyperscaler and colo customers, Carrier is working on both liquid and traditional cooling, combined through its Quantum Leap offering; the water- versus air-cooled choice depends on the customer's water access.

Carrier Energy / grid relief (CEO): the U.S. home energy management (HEMS) offering is "getting tremendous attention from hyperscalers and utilities". If Carrier's integrated heat pump and battery solution were in every home and building Carrier serves, it would free up nearly 15% of grid capacity during peak hours. Field trials have shown up to four hours of battery-powered heat pump operation during peak hours, with market launch planned later this year.
quarterly_data.figure: nearly 15% of grid capacity during peak hours; up to four hours of battery-powered heat pump operation; market launch later this year
